cond_0001.intro: We are looking for a General Engineer to join our team.
cond_0001.responsibilities:
Duties
Applies engineering knowledge to conventional engineering specific situations and participates in projects.
Assists higher grade scientists and engineers in engineering work.
Reviews tobacco products to determine the adequacy of the results from engineering disciplines.
Searches and reviews engineering literature to advance knowledge, participates in meetings, and participates in research projects conducted by senior engineers.
Supports higher-graded engineers/ scientists in their verbal and written conclusions to other Federal agencies, industry, universities, and state, local, and foreign governments.
Participates in the development of portions of new and amended regulations, policies, and procedures.
cond_0001.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
Completed all requirements for an associates, bachelors, masters, professional, doctorate, vocational, or technical degree or qualifying certificate from an accredited educational institution within the 2 years preceding the closing date of this announcement. -OR-
Released or discharged from active duty within the previous two years by 04/22/2024, where as a veteran who, due to a military service obligation, was precluded from applying to the Recent Graduate Program during any portion of the 2-year eligibility period following completion of degree or certificate requirements, are entitled to a full 2-year period of eligibility upon release or discharge from active duty. In no event, however, may the eligibility period extend beyond 6 years from the date on which the preference eligible veteran completed the requirements of the degree or certificate. -OR-
Expected to graduate with a qualifying Associate's, Bachelor's, Master's, Doctorate, professional, vocational or technical degree or certificate program by 06/30/2024. Current students must meet all eligibility and qualification requirements before a final offer can be made.
NOTE: You must submit transcripts or official documentation to verify your eligibility under the Recent Graduate Program. Transcripts MUST reflect the degree/certificate program and the degree conferred date. If your degree/certificate has not been conferred, you must provide proof of the anticipated graduation date. Selectee's entry on duty date will be upon degree conferment.
In addition to the eligibility requirements for the Pathways Recent Graduate Program, you must also meet the following Individual Occupational Requirements by 04/22/2024 in order to qualify for the General Engineer, 0801 positions.
Degree: Engineering. To be acceptable, the program must: (1) lead to a bachelor's degree in a school of engineering with at least one program accredited by ABET; or (2) include differential and integral calculus and courses (more advanced than first-year physics and chemistry) in five of the following seven areas of engineering science or physics: (a) statics, dynamics; (b) strength of materials (stress-strain relationships); (c) fluid mechanics, hydraulics; (d) thermodynamics; (e) electrical fields and circuits; (f) nature and properties of materials (relating particle and aggregate structure to properties); and (g) any other comparable area of fundamental engineering science or physics, such as optics, heat transfer, soil mechanics, or electronics. -OR-
Combination of education and experience -- college-level education, training, and/or technical experience that furnished (1) a thorough knowledge of the physical and mathematical sciences underlying engineering, and (2) a good understanding, both theoretical and practical, of the engineering sciences and techniques and their applications to one of the branches of engineering. The adequacy of such background must be demonstrated by one of the following:
Professional registration or licensure -- Current registration as an Engineer Intern (EI), Engineer in Training (EIT), or licensure as a Professional Engineer (PE) by any State, the District of Columbia, Guam, or Puerto Rico.
Written Test -- Evidence of having successfully passed the Fundamentals of Engineering (FE) examination or any other written test required for professional registration by an engineering licensure board in the various States, the District of Columbia, Guam, and Puerto Rico.
Specified academic courses -- Successful completion of at least 60 semester hours of courses in the physical, mathematical, and engineering sciences and that included the courses specified in the basic requirements under paragraph A.
Related curriculum -- Successful completion of a curriculum leading to a bachelor's degree in an appropriate scientific field, e.g., engineering technology, physics, chemistry, architecture, computer science, mathematics, hydrology, or geology, may be accepted in lieu of a bachelor's degree in engineering, provided the applicant has had at least 1 year of professional engineering experience acquired under professional engineering supervision and guidance.
For GS-7, applicants must meet one of the following by 04/22/2024:
At least one full year of specialized experience, equivalent to at least the GS-05 level in the Federal service which includes interpreting or reviewing scientific data. -OR-
Completion of one year of graduate level education related to the position being filled (Engineer) from an accredited college and/or university. -OR-
A bachelor's degree as described in the Basic Qualification Requirements above AND meet Superior Academic Achievement provision (S.A.A.) criteria. S.A.A. Is based on (1) class standing, (2) grade-point average, or (3) honor society membership. -OR-
A combination of experience and education that when combined equals 100% of the total requirements. -OR-
An engineering bachelor's degree AND appropriate specialized experience as an Engineering Technician. -OR-
Successfully completed a 5-year program of study of at least 160 semester hours leading to a bachelor's degree in engineering.
Preferred Requirements
For GS-9, applicants must meet one of the following by 04/22/2024:
At least one full year of specialized experience, equivalent to the GS-07 grade level in the Federal service which includes preparing scientific progress reports, presentations or conducting analysis. -OR-
2 Years of progressively higher level graduate education leading to a master's degree in Engineering or master's or equivalent graduate degree. -OR-
A combination of superior academic achievement AND one (1) year of appropriate specialized Engineering experience. -OR-
Successfully completed a 5-year program of study of at least 160 semester hours leading to a bachelor's degree in engineering AND one (1) year of appropriate professional Engineering experience.

To be considered, you should meet one of the following Recent Graduate Program eligibility paths:

B. A. A background in engineering — ideally a bachelor's degree from a program accredited by ABET, or equivalent coursework covering areas such as statics, dynamics, fluid mechanics, thermodynamics, electrical circuits, and materials science.
B. A combination of college-level education, training, and/or technical experience that provides a working knowledge of the physical and mathematical sciences underlying engineering, along with practical understanding of engineering techniques. Current registration as an Engineer Intern (EI), Engineer in Training (EIT), or licensure as a Professional Engineer (PE) by any State, the District of Columbia, Guam, or Puerto Rico.
Evidence of having passed the Fundamentals of Engineering (FE) examination or any other written test required for professional registration by an engineering licensure board.
Completion of at least 60 semester hours of courses in the physical, mathematical, and engineering sciences, including the courses specified under paragraph A above.
Completion of a curriculum leading to a bachelor's degree in a related scientific field (e.g., engineering technology, physics, chemistry, architecture, computer science, mathematics, hydrology, or geology), along with around 1 year of professional engineering experience acquired under professional engineering supervision and guidance.
Preferred Requirements
For GS-7, candidates should meet one of the following:
A. Around one year of specialized experience at or equivalent to the GS-05 level, including interpreting or reviewing scientific data, or an equivalent combination of education and experience.

C. A bachelor's degree as described above and meeting the Superior Academic Achievement (S.A.A.) criteria, based on class standing, grade-point average, or honor society membership.
D. A combination of experience as described in A and education as described in B that together equal 100% of the total requirements.
E. An engineering bachelor's degree and appropriate specialized experience as an Engineering Technician.
F. Successful completion of a 5-year program of at least 160 semester hours leading to a bachelor's degree in engineering.
For GS-9, candidates should meet one of the following:
A. Around one year of specialized experience equivalent to the GS-07 level, including preparing scientific progress reports, presentations, or conducting analysis, or an equivalent combination of education and experience.
B. Two years of progressively higher-level graduate education leading to a master's degree in Engineering, or a master's or equivalent graduate degree.
C. A combination of superior academic achievement and around one year of appropriate specialized engineering experience.
D. Successful completion of a 5-year program of at least 160 semester hours leading to a bachelor's degree in engineering, along with around one year of appropriate professional engineering experience.

cond_0027.responsibilities:
Work alongside higher-grade scientists and engineers on engineering projects, contributing your knowledge to conventional engineering situations.
Assist senior engineers in reviewing tobacco products to help determine the adequacy of results from engineering disciplines.
Search and review engineering literature to support shared knowledge-building, and participate in meetings and research projects led by senior engineers.
Help senior engineers and scientists communicate their verbal and written conclusions to other Federal agencies, industry, universities, and state, local, and foreign governments.
Collaborate in the development of portions of new and amended regulations, policies, and procedures.
cond_0027.requirements:
Applicants must meet the following eligibility requirements to participate in this Recent Graduate Program:
A. Completed all requirements for an associates, bachelors, masters, professional, doctorate, vocational, or technical degree or qualifying certificate from an accredited educational institution within the 2 years preceding the closing date of this announcement. -OR-
B. Released or discharged from active duty within the previous two years by 04/22/2024, where as a veteran who, due to a military service obligation, was precluded from applying to the Recent Graduate Program during any portion of the 2-year eligibility period following completion of degree or certificate requirements, are entitled to a full 2-year period of eligibility upon release or discharge from active duty. In no event, however, may the eligibility period extend beyond 6 years from the date on which the preference eligible veteran completed the requirements of the degree or certificate. -OR-
C. Individuals who are expected to graduate with a qualifying Associate's, Bachelor's, Master's, Doctorate, professional, vocational or technical degree or certificate program by 06/30/2024. Current students must meet all eligibility and qualification requirements before a final offer can be made.
NOTE: You must submit transcripts or official documentation to verify your eligibility under the Recent Graduate Program. Transcripts MUST reflect the degree/certificate program and the degree conferred date. If your degree/certificate has not been conferred, you must provide proof of the anticipated graduation date. Selectee's entry on duty date will be upon degree conferment.
Minimum Requirements
Engineering degree from a school with at least one ABET-accredited program; or a degree that includes differential and integral calculus and courses (more advanced than first-year physics and chemistry) in five of the following seven areas: (a) statics, dynamics; (b) strength of materials; (c) fluid mechanics, hydraulics; (d) thermodynamics; (e) electrical fields and circuits; (f) nature and properties of materials; (g) any other comparable area of fundamental engineering science or physics.
OR: Combination of college-level education, training, and/or technical experience demonstrating thorough knowledge of physical and mathematical sciences underlying engineering, evidenced by one of the following: current registration as an EI, EIT, or PE; passing the FE examination or equivalent written test; completion of at least 60 semester hours in physical, mathematical, and engineering sciences covering the courses in the basic requirements; or a bachelor's degree in a related scientific field (e.g., engineering technology, physics, chemistry, computer science, mathematics) plus at least 1 year of professional engineering experience under professional supervision.
For GS-7 (one of the following):
At least one full year of specialized experience equivalent to GS-05, including interpreting or reviewing scientific data.
One year of graduate-level education related to engineering from an accredited institution.
A qualifying bachelor's degree meeting Superior Academic Achievement (S.A.A.) criteria based on class standing, GPA, or honor society membership.
A combination of the experience and education above totaling 100%.
An engineering bachelor's degree plus appropriate specialized experience as an Engineering Technician.
Successful completion of a 5-year program of at least 160 semester hours leading to a bachelor's degree in engineering.
For GS-9 (one of the following):
At least one full year of specialized experience equivalent to GS-07, including preparing scientific progress reports, presentations, or conducting analysis.
Two years of progressively higher-level graduate education leading to a master's degree in Engineering, or a master's or equivalent graduate degree.
A combination of superior academic achievement and one year of appropriate specialized engineering experience.
A 5-year program of at least 160 semester hours leading to a bachelor's degree in engineering, plus one year of appropriate professional engineering experience.
Preferred Requirements
Familiarity with regulatory or policy development processes.
Experience communicating technical findings in written or verbal form to external stakeholders.

cond_0028.responsibilities:
Applies engineering knowledge to conventional engineering specific situations and participates in projects.
Assists higher grade scientists and engineers in engineering work.
Reviews tobacco products to determine the adequacy of the results from engineering disciplines.
Searches and reviews engineering literature to advance knowledge, participates in meetings, and participates in research projects conducted by senior engineers.

Participates in the development of portions of new and amended regulations, policies, and procedures.
cond_0028.requirements:
Applicants must meet the following eligibility requirements to participate in this Recent Graduate Program:
A. Completed all requirements for an associates, bachelors, masters, professional, doctorate, vocational, or technical degree or qualifying certificate from an accredited educational institution within the 2 years preceding the closing date of this announcement. -OR-
B. Released or discharged from active duty within the previous two years by 04/22/2024, where as a veteran who, due to a military service obligation, was precluded from applying to the Recent Graduate Program during any portion of the 2-year eligibility period following completion of degree or certificate requirements, are entitled to a full 2-year period of eligibility upon release or discharge from active duty. In no event, however, may the eligibility period extend beyond 6 years from the date on which the preference eligible veteran completed the requirements of the degree or certificate. -OR-
C. Individuals who are expected to graduate with a qualifying Associate's, Bachelor's, Master's, Doctorate, professional, vocational or technical degree or certificate program by 06/30/2024. Current students must meet all eligibility and qualification requirements before a final offer can be made.
NOTE: You must submit transcripts or official documentation to verify your eligibility under the Recent Graduate Program. Transcripts MUST reflect the degree/certificate program and the degree conferred date. If your degree/certificate has not been conferred, you must provide proof of the anticipated graduation date. Selectee's entry on duty date will be upon degree conferment.
In addition to the eligibility requirements for the Pathways Recent Graduate Program, you must also meet the following Individual Occupational Requirements by 04/22/2024 in order to qualify for the General Engineer, 0801 positions.
A. Degree: Engineering. To be acceptable, the program must: (1) lead to a bachelor's degree in a school of engineering with at least one program accredited by ABET; or (2) include differential and integral calculus and courses (more advanced than first-year physics and chemistry) in five of the following seven areas of engineering science or physics: (a) statics, dynamics; (b) strength of materials (stress-strain relationships); (c) fluid mechanics, hydraulics; (d) thermodynamics; (e) electrical fields and circuits; (f) nature and properties of materials (relating particle and aggregate structure to properties); and (g) any other comparable area of fundamental engineering science or physics, such as optics, heat transfer, soil mechanics, or electronics. -OR-
B. Combination of education and experience -- college-level education, training, and/or technical experience that furnished (1) a thorough knowledge of the physical and mathematical sciences underlying engineering, and (2) a good understanding, both theoretical and practical, of the engineering sciences and techniques and their applications to one of the branches of engineering. The adequacy of such background must be demonstrated by one of the following:
Professional registration or licensure -- Current registration as an Engineer Intern (EI), Engineer in Training (EIT), or licensure as a Professional Engineer (PE) by any State, the District of Columbia, Guam, or Puerto Rico. Absent other means of qualifying under this standard, those applicants who achieved such registration by means other than written test (e.g., State grandfather or eminence provisions) are eligible only for positions that are within or closely related to the specialty field of their registration. For example, an applicant who attains registration through a State Board's eminence provision as a manufacturing engineer typically would be rated eligible only for manufacturing engineering positions.
Written Test -- Evidence of having successfully passed the Fundamentals of Engineering (FE) examination or any other written test required for professional registration by an engineering licensure board in the various States, the District of Columbia, Guam, and Puerto Rico.
Specified academic courses -- Successful completion of at least 60 semester hours of courses in the physical, mathematical, and engineering sciences and that included the courses specified in the basic requirements under paragraph A. The courses must be fully acceptable toward meeting the requirements of an engineering program as described in paragraph A.
Related curriculum -- Successful completion of a curriculum leading to a bachelor's degree in an appropriate scientific field, e.g., engineering technology, physics, chemistry, architecture, computer science, mathematics, hydrology, or geology, may be accepted in lieu of a bachelor's degree in engineering, provided the applicant has had at least 1 year of professional engineering experience acquired under professional engineering supervision and guidance. Ordinarily there should be either an established plan of intensive training to develop professional engineering competence, or several years of prior professional engineering-type experience, e.g., in interdisciplinary positions. (The above examples of related curricula are not all-inclusive.)
In addition to meeting the Individual Occupational Requirements above, you must also meet the OPM Qualification Requirements listed below by 04/22/2024 in order to qualify for the General Engineer, 0801, at GS-7/9.
For GS-7:
A. Applicants must have at least one full year of specialized experience, equivalent to at least the GS-05 level in the Federal service which includes interpreting or reviewing scientific data. -OR-
B. Completion of one year of graduate level education related to the position being filled (Engineer) from an accredited college and/or university. -OR-
C. A bachelor's degree as described in the Basic Qualification Requirements above AND meet Superior Academic Achievement provision (S.A.A.) criteria. S.A.A. Is based on (1) class standing, (2) grade-point average, or (3) honor society membership. -OR-
D. Have a combination of experience as described in ""A"" above and education as described in ""B"" above, that when combined equals 100% of the total requirements. -OR-
E. Have an engineering bachelor's degree AND have appropriate specialized experience as an Engineering Technician. -OR-
F. Have successfully completed a 5-year program of study of at least 160 semester hours leading to a bachelor's degree in engineering.
For GS-9:
A. Applicants must have at least one full year of specialized experience, equivalent to the GS-07 grade level in the Federal service which includes preparing scientific progress reports, presentations or conducting analysis. -OR-
B. Have 2 years of progressively higher level graduate education leading to a master's degree in Engineering or master's or equivalent graduate degree. -OR-
C. Have a combination of superior academic achievement AND one (1) year of appropriate specialized Engineering experience. -OR-
D. Have successfully completed a 5-year program of study of at least 160 semester hours leading to a bachelor's degree in engineering AND have one (1) year of appropriate professional Engineering experience.

Applies engineering knowledge to conventional engineering specific situations and participates in projects.
Assists higher grade scientists and engineers in engineering work.
Reviews tobacco products to determine the adequacy of the results from engineering disciplines.
Searches and reviews engineering literature to advance knowledge, participates in meetings, and participates in research projects conducted by senior engineers.
Supports higher-graded engineers/ scientists in their verbal and written conclusions to other Federal agencies, industry, universities, and state, local, and foreign governments.
Participates in the development of portions of new and amended regulations, policies, and procedures.
cond_0047.requirements:
Applicants must demonstrate they meet the following eligibility requirements to participate in this Recent Graduate Program:
A. Completed all requirements for an associates, bachelors, masters, professional, doctorate, vocational, or technical degree or qualifying certificate from an accredited educational institution within the 2 years preceding the closing date of this announcement. -OR-
B. Released or discharged from active duty within the previous two years by 04/22/2024, where as a veteran who, due to a military service obligation, was precluded from applying to the Recent Graduate Program during any portion of the 2-year eligibility period following completion of degree or certificate requirements, are entitled to a full 2-year period of eligibility upon release or discharge from active duty. In no event, however, may the eligibility period extend beyond 6 years from the date on which the preference eligible veteran completed the requirements of the degree or certificate. -OR-
C. Individuals who are expected to graduate with a qualifying Associate's, Bachelor's, Master's, Doctorate, professional, vocational or technical degree or certificate program by 06/30/2024. Current students must meet all eligibility and qualification requirements before a final offer can be made.
NOTE: You must submit transcripts or official documentation to verify your eligibility under the Recent Graduate Program. Transcripts MUST reflect the degree/certificate program and the degree conferred date. If your degree/certificate has not been conferred, you must provide proof of the anticipated graduation date. Selectee's entry on duty date will be upon degree conferment.
In addition to the eligibility requirements for the Pathways Recent Graduate Program, you must also demonstrate deep knowledge of engineering fundamentals and meet the following Individual Occupational Requirements by 04/22/2024 in order to qualify for the General Engineer, 0801 positions.
A. Degree: Engineering. To be acceptable, the program must: (1) lead to a bachelor's degree in a school of engineering with at least one program accredited by ABET; or (2) include differential and integral calculus and courses (more advanced than first-year physics and chemistry) in five of the following seven areas of engineering science or physics: (a) statics, dynamics; (b) strength of materials (stress-strain relationships); (c) fluid mechanics, hydraulics; (d) thermodynamics; (e) electrical fields and circuits; (f) nature and properties of materials (relating particle and aggregate structure to properties); and (g) any other comparable area of fundamental engineering science or physics, such as optics, heat transfer, soil mechanics, or electronics. -OR-
B. Combination of education and experience -- college-level education, training, and/or technical experience that furnished (1) a thorough knowledge of the physical and mathematical sciences underlying engineering, and (2) a solid understanding, both theoretical and practical, of the engineering sciences and techniques and their applications to one of the branches of engineering. The adequacy of such background must be demonstrated by one of the following:
Professional registration or licensure -- Current registration as an Engineer Intern (EI), Engineer in Training (EIT), or licensure as a Professional Engineer (PE) by any State, the District of Columbia, Guam, or Puerto Rico. Absent other means of qualifying under this standard, those applicants who achieved such registration by means other than written test (e.g., State grandfather or eminence provisions) are eligible only for positions that are within or closely related to the specialty field of their registration.
Written Test -- Evidence of having successfully passed the Fundamentals of Engineering (FE) examination or any other written test required for professional registration by an engineering licensure board in the various States, the District of Columbia, Guam, and Puerto Rico.
Specified academic courses -- Successful completion of at least 60 semester hours of courses in the physical, mathematical, and engineering sciences and that included the courses specified in the basic requirements under paragraph A. The courses must be fully acceptable toward meeting the requirements of an engineering program as described in paragraph A.
Related curriculum -- Successful completion of a curriculum leading to a bachelor's degree in an appropriate scientific field, e.g., engineering technology, physics, chemistry, architecture, computer science, mathematics, hydrology, or geology, may be accepted in lieu of a bachelor's degree in engineering, provided the applicant has demonstrated at least 1 year of professional engineering experience acquired under professional engineering supervision and guidance. Ordinarily there should be either an established plan of intensive training to develop professional engineering competence, or several years of prior professional engineering-type experience, e.g., in interdisciplinary positions.
In addition to meeting the Individual Occupational Requirements above, you must also meet the OPM Qualification Requirements listed below by 04/22/2024 in order to qualify for the General Engineer, 0801, at GS-7/9.
For GS-7:
A. Applicants must have demonstrated at least one full year of specialized experience, equivalent to at least the GS-05 level in the Federal service, with a proven track record of interpreting or reviewing scientific data. -OR-
B. Completion of one year of graduate level education related to the position being filled (Engineer) from an accredited college and/or university. -OR-
C. A bachelor's degree as described in the Basic Qualification Requirements above AND meet Superior Academic Achievement provision (S.A.A.) criteria. S.A.A. Is based on (1) class standing, (2) grade-point average, or (3) honor society membership. -OR-
D. Have a combination of experience as described in ""A"" above and education as described in ""B"" above, that when combined equals 100% of the total requirements. -OR-
E. Have an engineering bachelor's degree AND have demonstrated appropriate specialized experience as an Engineering Technician. -OR-
F. Have successfully completed a 5-year program of study of at least 160 semester hours leading to a bachelor's degree in engineering.
For GS-9:
A. Applicants must have demonstrated at least one full year of specialized experience, equivalent to the GS-07 grade level in the Federal service, with a proven track record of preparing scientific progress reports, presentations or conducting analysis. -OR-
B. Have 2 years of progressively higher level graduate education leading to a master's degree in Engineering or master's or equivalent graduate degree; advanced degree strongly preferred. -OR-
C. Have a combination of superior academic achievement AND one (1) year of appropriate specialized Engineering experience. -OR-
D. Have successfully completed a 5-year program of study of at least 160 semester hours leading to a bachelor's degree in engineering AND have demonstrated one (1) year of appropriate professional Engineering experience.

Lead coordination with senior scientists and engineers on engineering tasks.
Review tobacco products to determine the adequacy of results from engineering disciplines.
Search and review engineering literature to advance knowledge, drive participation in meetings, and execute research projects led by senior engineers.
Deliver verbal and written conclusions to other Federal agencies, industry, universities, and state, local, and foreign governments in support of higher-graded engineers and scientists.

cond_0071.requirements:
Applicants must meet the following eligibility requirements to participate in this Recent Graduate Program:
A. Completed all requirements for an associates, bachelors, masters, professional, doctorate, vocational, or technical degree or qualifying certificate from an accredited educational institution within the 2 years preceding the closing date of this announcement. -OR-
B. Released or discharged from active duty within the previous two years by 04/22/2024, where as a veteran who, due to a military service obligation, was precluded from applying to the Recent Graduate Program during any portion of the 2-year eligibility period following completion of degree or certificate requirements, are entitled to a full 2-year period of eligibility upon release or discharge from active duty. In no event, however, may the eligibility period extend beyond 6 years from the date on which the preference eligible veteran completed the requirements of the degree or certificate. -OR-
C. Individuals who are expected to graduate with a qualifying Associate's, Bachelor's, Master's, Doctorate, professional, vocational or technical degree or certificate program by 06/30/2024. Current students must meet all eligibility and qualification requirements before a final offer can be made.
NOTE: You must submit transcripts or official documentation to verify your eligibility under the Recent Graduate Program. Transcripts MUST reflect the degree/certificate program and the degree conferred date. If your degree/certificate has not been conferred, you must provide proof of the anticipated graduation date. Selectee's entry on duty date will be upon degree conferment.
In addition to the eligibility requirements for the Pathways Recent Graduate Program, you must also meet the following Individual Occupational Requirements by 04/22/2024 in order to qualify for the General Engineer, 0801 positions.
A. Degree: Engineering. To be acceptable, the program must: (1) lead to a bachelor's degree in a school of engineering with at least one program accredited by ABET; or (2) include differential and integral calculus and courses (more advanced than first-year physics and chemistry) in five of the following seven areas of engineering science or physics: (a) statics, dynamics; (b) strength of materials (stress-strain relationships); (c) fluid mechanics, hydraulics; (d) thermodynamics; (e) electrical fields and circuits; (f) nature and properties of materials (relating particle and aggregate structure to properties); and (g) any other comparable area of fundamental engineering science or physics, such as optics, heat transfer, soil mechanics, or electronics. -OR-
B. Combination of education and experience -- college-level education, training, and/or technical experience that furnished (1) a thorough knowledge of the physical and mathematical sciences underlying engineering, and (2) a good understanding, both theoretical and practical, of the engineering sciences and techniques and their applications to one of the branches of engineering. The adequacy of such background must be demonstrated by one of the following:
Professional registration or licensure -- Current registration as an Engineer Intern (EI), Engineer in Training (EIT), or licensure as a Professional Engineer (PE) by any State, the District of Columbia, Guam, or Puerto Rico. Absent other means of qualifying under this standard, those applicants who achieved such registration by means other than written test (e.g., State grandfather or eminence provisions) are eligible only for positions that are within or closely related to the specialty field of their registration. For example, an applicant who attains registration through a State Board's eminence provision as a manufacturing engineer typically would be rated eligible only for manufacturing engineering positions.
Written Test -- Evidence of having successfully passed the Fundamentals of Engineering (FE) examination or any other written test required for professional registration by an engineering licensure board in the various States, the District of Columbia, Guam, and Puerto Rico.
Specified academic courses -- Successful completion of at least 60 semester hours of courses in the physical, mathematical, and engineering sciences and that included the courses specified in the basic requirements under paragraph A. The courses must be fully acceptable toward meeting the requirements of an engineering program as described in paragraph A.
Related curriculum -- Successful completion of a curriculum leading to a bachelor's degree in an appropriate scientific field, e.g., engineering technology, physics, chemistry, architecture, computer science, mathematics, hydrology, or geology, may be accepted in lieu of a bachelor's degree in engineering, provided the applicant has had at least 1 year of professional engineering experience acquired under professional engineering supervision and guidance. Ordinarily there should be either an established plan of intensive training to develop professional engineering competence, or several years of prior professional engineering-type experience, e.g., in interdisciplinary positions. (The above examples of related curricula are not all-inclusive.)
In addition to meeting the Individual Occupational Requirements above, you must also meet the OPM Qualification Requirements listed below by 04/22/2024 in order to qualify for the General Engineer, 0801, at GS-7/9.
For GS-7:
A. Applicants must have at least one full year of specialized experience, equivalent to at least the GS-05 level in the Federal service which includes interpreting or reviewing scientific data. -OR-
B. Completion of one year of graduate level education related to the position being filled (Engineer) from an accredited college and/or university. -OR-
C. A bachelor's degree as described in the Basic Qualification Requirements above AND meet Superior Academic Achievement provision (S.A.A.) criteria. S.A.A. Is based on (1) class standing, (2) grade-point average, or (3) honor society membership. -OR-
D. Have a combination of experience as described in ""A"" above and education as described in ""B"" above, that when combined equals 100% of the total requirements. -OR-
E. Have an engineering bachelor's degree AND have appropriate specialized experience as an Engineering Technician. -OR-
F. Have successfully completed a 5-year program of study of at least 160 semester hours leading to a bachelor's degree in engineering.
For GS-9:
A. Applicants must have at least one full year of specialized experience, equivalent to the GS-07 grade level in the Federal service which includes preparing scientific progress reports, presentations or conducting analysis. -OR-
B. Have 2 years of progressively higher level graduate education leading to a master's degree in Engineering or master's or equivalent graduate degree. -OR-
C. Have a combination of superior academic achievement AND one (1) year of appropriate specialized Engineering experience. -OR-
D. Have successfully completed a 5-year program of study of at least 160 semester hours leading to a bachelor's degree in engineering AND have one (1) year of appropriate professional Engineering experience.

cond_0087.requirements:

B. Released or discharged from active duty within the previous two years by 04/22/2024, where as a veteran who, due to a military service obligation, was precluded from applying to the Recent Graduate Program during any portion of the 2-year eligibility period following completion of degree or certificate requirements, are entitled to a full 2-year period of eligibility upon release or discharge from active duty. B. Have 2 years of progressively higher level graduate education leading to a master's degree in Engineering or master's or equivalent graduate degree. -OR-
C. Have a combination of superior academic achievement AND one (1) year of appropriate specialized Engineering experience. -OR-

cond_0119.requirements:

A. Completed all requirements for an associates, bachelors, masters, professional, doctorate, vocational, or technical degree or qualifying certificate from an accredited educational institution within the 2 years preceding the closing date of this announcement. -OR-

Released or discharged from active duty within the previous two years by 04/22/2024, where as a veteran who, due to a military service obligation, was precluded from applying to the Recent Graduate Program during any portion of the 2-year eligibility period following completion of degree or certificate requirements, are entitled to a full 2-year period of eligibility upon release or discharge from active duty. A. Degree: Engineering. D. Have a combination of experience as described in ""A"" above and education as described in ""B"" above, that when combined equals 100% of the total requirements. -OR-
E. Have an engineering bachelor's degree AND have demonstrated appropriate specialized experience as an Engineering Technician. -OR-
F. Have successfully completed a 5-year program of study of at least 160 semester hours leading to a bachelor's degree in engineering.
For GS-9:
A. Applicants must have demonstrated at least one full year of specialized experience, equivalent to the GS-07 grade level in the Federal service, with a proven track record of preparing scientific progress reports, presentations or conducting analysis. -OR-

C. Have a combination of superior academic achievement AND one (1) year of appropriate specialized Engineering experience. -OR-

A. Completed all requirements for an associates, bachelors, masters, professional, doctorate, vocational, or technical degree or qualifying certificate from an accredited educational institution within the 2 years preceding the closing date of this announcement. -OR-
B. Released or discharged from active duty within the previous two years by 04/22/2024, where as a veteran who, due to a military service obligation, was precluded from applying to the Recent Graduate Program during any portion of the 2-year eligibility period following completion of degree or certificate requirements, are entitled to a full 2-year period of eligibility upon release or discharge from active duty. In no event, however, may the eligibility period extend beyond 6 years from the date on which the preference eligible veteran completed the requirements of the degree or certificate. -OR-
C. Individuals who are expected to graduate with a qualifying Associate's, Bachelor's, Master's, Doctorate, professional, vocational or technical degree or certificate program by 06/30/2024. Current students must meet all eligibility and qualification requirements before a final offer can be made.
NOTE: You must submit transcripts or official documentation to verify your eligibility under the Recent Graduate Program. Transcripts MUST reflect the degree/certificate program and the degree conferred date. If your degree/certificate has not been conferred, you must provide proof of the anticipated graduation date. Selectee's entry on duty date will be upon degree conferment.
Minimum Requirements
Engineering degree from a school with at least one ABET-accredited program; or a degree that included differential and integral calculus and courses (more advanced than first-year physics and chemistry) in five of the following seven areas: (a) statics, dynamics; (b) strength of materials (stress-strain relationships); (c) fluid mechanics, hydraulics; (d) thermodynamics; (e) electrical fields and circuits; (f) nature and properties of materials (relating particle and aggregate structure to properties); and (g) any other comparable area of fundamental engineering science or physics, such as optics, heat transfer, soil mechanics, or electronics.
For GS-7: At least one full year of specialized experience equivalent to GS-05 level which includes interpreting or reviewing scientific data; OR completion of one year of graduate level education related to Engineering from an accredited college and/or university; OR a bachelor's degree meeting the Basic Qualification Requirements above AND Superior Academic Achievement (S.A.A.) criteria based on (1) class standing, (2) grade-point average, or (3) honor society membership; OR a combination of the above experience and education that when combined equals 100% of the total requirements; OR an engineering bachelor's degree AND appropriate specialized experience as an Engineering Technician; OR successful completion of a 5-year program of study of at least 160 semester hours leading to a bachelor's degree in engineering.
For GS-9: At least one full year of specialized experience equivalent to GS-07 level which includes preparing scientific progress reports, presentations or conducting analysis; OR 2 years of progressively higher level graduate education leading to a master's degree in Engineering or master's or equivalent graduate degree; OR a combination of superior academic achievement AND one (1) year of appropriate specialized Engineering experience; OR successful completion of a 5-year program of study of at least 160 semester hours leading to a bachelor's degree in engineering AND one (1) year of appropriate professional Engineering experience.
Preferred Requirements
Combination of college-level education, training, and/or technical experience that furnished (1) a thorough knowledge of the physical and mathematical sciences underlying engineering, and (2) a good understanding, both theoretical and practical, of the engineering sciences and techniques and their applications to one of the branches of engineering, demonstrated by one of the following:
Current registration as an Engineer Intern (EI), Engineer in Training (EIT), or licensure as a Professional Engineer (PE) by any State, the District of Columbia, Guam, or Puerto Rico.
Evidence of having successfully passed the Fundamentals of Engineering (FE) examination or any other written test required for professional registration by an engineering licensure board.
Successful completion of at least 60 semester hours of courses in the physical, mathematical, and engineering sciences including the courses specified in the basic requirements.
Successful completion of a curriculum leading to a bachelor's degree in an appropriate scientific field (e.g., engineering technology, physics, chemistry, architecture, computer science, mathematics, hydrology, or geology), provided the applicant has had at least 1 year of professional engineering experience acquired under professional engineering supervision and guidance.

cond_0150.intro: We are looking for a General Engineer (Recent Graduate) to join our team.
cond_0150.responsibilities:
A large part of this role involves staying engaged with colleagues, senior engineers, and external contacts on a regular basis.
Apply engineering knowledge to conventional engineering situations and actively contribute to projects.
Work closely with higher-grade scientists and engineers on engineering tasks, communicating regularly to support their work.
Review tobacco products to determine the adequacy of results from engineering disciplines.
Search and review engineering literature to advance knowledge, participate in meetings, and contribute to research projects led by senior engineers.
Support higher-graded engineers and scientists in communicating verbal and written conclusions to other Federal agencies, industry, universities, and state, local, and foreign governments — including helping to clarify findings and handle questions from these groups.
Participate in the development of portions of new and amended regulations, policies, and procedures, actively contributing your perspective during team discussions.

Recent Graduate Program Eligibility (one of the following):
Completed all requirements for an associate's, bachelor's, master's, professional, doctorate, vocational, or technical degree or qualifying certificate from an accredited institution within the 2 years preceding the closing date.
Released or discharged from active duty within the previous two years by 04/22/2024, where as a veteran who, due to a military service obligation, was precluded from applying during any portion of the 2-year eligibility period following degree or certificate completion, and is entitled to a full 2-year period of eligibility upon release or discharge. In no event may the eligibility period extend beyond 6 years from the date the preference eligible veteran completed the degree or certificate requirements.
Expected to graduate with a qualifying degree or certificate by 06/30/2024. Must meet all eligibility and qualification requirements before a final offer can be made.

If your degree has not been conferred, provide proof of the anticipated graduation date. Entry on duty date will be upon degree conferment.

At least one full year of specialized experience equivalent to GS-05, including interpreting or reviewing scientific data.

Bachelor's degree meeting the basic qualification requirements above AND Superior Academic Achievement (based on class standing, GPA, or honor society membership).
A combination of experience and education as described above that together equals 100% of total requirements.
Engineering bachelor's degree AND appropriate specialized experience as an Engineering Technician.
Completed a 5-year program of at least 160 semester hours leading to a bachelor's degree in engineering.
GS-9 (one of the following):

Two years of progressively higher-level graduate education leading to a master's degree in Engineering, or a master's or equivalent graduate degree.
Superior academic achievement AND one year of appropriate specialized engineering experience.
Completed a 5-year program of at least 160 semester hours leading to a bachelor's degree in engineering AND one year of appropriate professional engineering experience.
Preferred Requirements
Familiarity with regulatory development processes or policy work.
Experience supporting written or verbal communications to external organizations such as government agencies, industry, or universities.

A. Applicants must have demonstrated at least one full year of specialized experience, equivalent to the GS-07 grade level in the Federal service, with a proven track record of preparing scientific progress reports, presentations or conducting analysis. -OR-

cond_0175.intro: We are looking for a General Engineer to join our team. This is a Recent Graduate Program position. People who do well in this role are often quick to grasp the kind of engineering and scientific problems the work involves.
cond_0175.responsibilities:
Applies engineering knowledge to conventional engineering specific situations and participates in projects.
Assists higher grade scientists and engineers in engineering work.
Reviews tobacco products to determine the adequacy of the results from engineering disciplines.
Searches and reviews engineering literature to advance knowledge, participates in meetings, and participates in research projects conducted by senior engineers.
Supports higher-graded engineers/ scientists in their verbal and written conclusions to other Federal agencies, industry, universities, and state, local, and foreign governments.
Participates in the development of portions of new and amended regulations, policies, and procedures.
cond_0175.requirements:
Applicants must meet the following eligibility requirements to participate in this Recent Graduate Program:
A. Completed all requirements for an associates, bachelors, masters, professional, doctorate, vocational, or technical degree or qualifying certificate from an accredited educational institution within the 2 years preceding the closing date of this announcement. -OR-
B. Released or discharged from active duty within the previous two years by 04/22/2024, where as a veteran who, due to a military service obligation, was precluded from applying to the Recent Graduate Program during any portion of the 2-year eligibility period following completion of degree or certificate requirements, are entitled to a full 2-year period of eligibility upon release or discharge from active duty. In no event, however, may the eligibility period extend beyond 6 years from the date on which the preference eligible veteran completed the requirements of the degree or certificate. -OR-
C. Individuals who are expected to graduate with a qualifying Associate's, Bachelor's, Master's, Doctorate, professional, vocational or technical degree or certificate program by 06/30/2024. Current students must meet all eligibility and qualification requirements before a final offer can be made.
NOTE: You must submit transcripts or official documentation to verify your eligibility under the Recent Graduate Program. Transcripts MUST reflect the degree/certificate program and the degree conferred date. If your degree/certificate has not been conferred, you must provide proof of the anticipated graduation date. Selectee's entry on duty date will be upon degree conferment.
In addition to the eligibility requirements for the Pathways Recent Graduate Program, you must also meet the following Individual Occupational Requirements by 04/22/2024 in order to qualify for the General Engineer, 0801 positions.
A. Degree: Engineering. To be acceptable, the program must: (1) lead to a bachelor's degree in a school of engineering with at least one program accredited by ABET; or (2) include differential and integral calculus and courses (more advanced than first-year physics and chemistry) in five of the following seven areas of engineering science or physics: (a) statics, dynamics; (b) strength of materials (stress-strain relationships); (c) fluid mechanics, hydraulics; (d) thermodynamics; (e) electrical fields and circuits; (f) nature and properties of materials (relating particle and aggregate structure to properties); and (g) any other comparable area of fundamental engineering science or physics, such as optics, heat transfer, soil mechanics, or electronics. -OR-
B. Combination of education and experience -- college-level education, training, and/or technical experience that furnished (1) a thorough knowledge of the physical and mathematical sciences underlying engineering, and (2) a good understanding, both theoretical and practical, of the engineering sciences and techniques and their applications to one of the branches of engineering. The adequacy of such background must be demonstrated by one of the following:
Professional registration or licensure -- Current registration as an Engineer Intern (EI), Engineer in Training (EIT), or licensure as a Professional Engineer (PE) by any State, the District of Columbia, Guam, or Puerto Rico. Absent other means of qualifying under this standard, those applicants who achieved such registration by means other than written test (e.g., State grandfather or eminence provisions) are eligible only for positions that are within or closely related to the specialty field of their registration. For example, an applicant who attains registration through a State Board's eminence provision as a manufacturing engineer typically would be rated eligible only for manufacturing engineering positions.
Written Test -- Evidence of having successfully passed the Fundamentals of Engineering (FE) examination or any other written test required for professional registration by an engineering licensure board in the various States, the District of Columbia, Guam, and Puerto Rico.

Related curriculum -- Successful completion of a curriculum leading to a bachelor's degree in an appropriate scientific field, e.g., engineering technology, physics, chemistry, architecture, computer science, mathematics, hydrology, or geology, may be accepted in lieu of a bachelor's degree in engineering, provided the applicant has had at least 1 year of professional engineering experience acquired under professional engineering supervision and guidance. (The above examples of related curricula are not all-inclusive.)

D. Have a combination of experience as described in ""A"" above and education as described in ""B"" above, that when combined equals 100% of the total requirements. -OR-
E. Have an engineering bachelor's degree AND have appropriate specialized experience as an Engineering Technician. -OR-
F. Have successfully completed a 5-year program of study of at least 160 semester hours leading to a bachelor's degree in engineering.
For GS-9:
A. Applicants must have at least one full year of specialized experience, equivalent to the GS-07 grade level in the Federal service which includes preparing scientific progress reports, presentations or conducting analysis. -OR-
B. Have 2 years of progressively higher level graduate education leading to a master's degree in Engineering or master's or equivalent graduate degree. -OR-
C. Have a combination of superior academic achievement AND one (1) year of appropriate specialized Engineering experience. -OR-
D. Have successfully completed a 5-year program of study of at least 160 semester hours leading to a bachelor's degree in engineering AND have one (1) year of appropriate professional Engineering experience.

B. Combination of education and experience -- college-level education, training, and/or technical experience that furnished (1) a thorough knowledge of the physical and mathematical sciences underlying engineering, and (2) a good understanding, both theoretical and practical, of the engineering sciences and techniques and their applications to one of the branches of engineering. Professional registration or licensure -- Current registration as an Engineer Intern (EI), Engineer in Training (EIT), or licensure as a Professional Engineer (PE) by any State, the District of Columbia, Guam, or Puerto Rico. cond_0191.intro: This is a Recent Graduate Program opportunity. The position is open to recent graduates who meet the eligibility requirements described below.
cond_0191.responsibilities:
Applies engineering knowledge to conventional engineering specific situations and participates in projects.
Assists higher grade scientists and engineers in engineering work.
Reviews tobacco products to determine the adequacy of the results from engineering disciplines.
Searches and reviews engineering literature to advance knowledge, participates in meetings, and participates in research projects conducted by senior engineers.
Supports higher-graded engineers/ scientists in their verbal and written conclusions to other Federal agencies, industry, universities, and state, local, and foreign governments.
Participates in the development of portions of new and amended regulations, policies, and procedures.
cond_0191.requirements:
Applicants must demonstrate they meet the following eligibility requirements to participate in this Recent Graduate Program:
A. Completed all requirements for an associates, bachelors, masters, professional, doctorate, vocational, or technical degree or qualifying certificate from an accredited educational institution within the 2 years preceding the closing date of this announcement. -OR-
B. Released or discharged from active duty within the previous two years by 04/22/2024, where as a veteran who, due to a military service obligation, was precluded from applying to the Recent Graduate Program during any portion of the 2-year eligibility period following completion of degree or certificate requirements, are entitled to a full 2-year period of eligibility upon release or discharge from active duty. In no event, however, may the eligibility period extend beyond 6 years from the date on which the preference eligible veteran completed the requirements of the degree or certificate. -OR-
C. Individuals who are expected to graduate with a qualifying Associate's, Bachelor's, Master's, Doctorate, professional, vocational or technical degree or certificate program by 06/30/2024. Current students must meet all eligibility and qualification requirements before a final offer can be made.
NOTE: You must submit transcripts or official documentation to verify your eligibility under the Recent Graduate Program. Transcripts MUST reflect the degree/certificate program and the degree conferred date. If your degree/certificate has not been conferred, you must provide proof of the anticipated graduation date. Selectee's entry on duty date will be upon degree conferment.

A. Degree: Engineering. B. Combination of education and experience -- college-level education, training, and/or technical experience that furnished (1) a thorough knowledge of the physical and mathematical sciences underlying engineering, and (2) a solid understanding, both theoretical and practical, of the engineering sciences and techniques and their applications to one of the branches of engineering. Professional registration or licensure -- Current registration as an Engineer Intern (EI), Engineer in Training (EIT), or licensure as a Professional Engineer (PE) by any State, the District of Columbia, Guam, or Puerto Rico. For GS-9:
A. Applicants must have demonstrated at least one full year of specialized experience, equivalent to the GS-07 grade level in the Federal service, with a proven track record of preparing scientific progress reports, presentations or conducting analysis. -OR-
B. Have 2 years of progressively higher level graduate education leading to a master's degree in Engineering or master's or equivalent graduate degree; advanced degree strongly preferred. -OR-
C. Have a combination of superior academic achievement AND one (1) year of appropriate specialized Engineering experience. -OR-
D. Have successfully completed a 5-year program of study of at least 160 semester hours leading to a bachelor's degree in engineering AND have demonstrated one (1) year of appropriate professional Engineering experience.

cond_0263.intro: This is a Recent Graduate Program opportunity. The position is open to recent graduates who meet the eligibility requirements described below.
cond_0263.responsibilities:
Applies engineering knowledge to conventional engineering specific situations and participates in projects.
Assists higher grade scientists and engineers in engineering work.
Reviews tobacco products to determine the adequacy of the results from engineering disciplines.
Searches and reviews engineering literature to advance knowledge, participates in meetings, and participates in research projects conducted by senior engineers.
Supports higher-graded engineers/ scientists in their verbal and written conclusions to other Federal agencies, industry, universities, and state, local, and foreign governments.
Participates in the development of portions of new and amended regulations, policies, and procedures.
cond_0263.requirements:
Applicants must demonstrate they meet the following eligibility requirements to participate in this Recent Graduate Program:
A. Completed all requirements for an associates, bachelors, masters, professional, doctorate, vocational, or technical degree or qualifying certificate from an accredited educational institution within the 2 years preceding the closing date of this announcement. -OR-
B. Released or discharged from active duty within the previous two years by 04/22/2024, where as a veteran who, due to a military service obligation, was precluded from applying to the Recent Graduate Program during any portion of the 2-year eligibility period following completion of degree or certificate requirements, are entitled to a full 2-year period of eligibility upon release or discharge from active duty. In no event, however, may the eligibility period extend beyond 6 years from the date on which the preference eligible veteran completed the requirements of the degree or certificate. -OR-
C. Individuals who are expected to graduate with a qualifying Associate's, Bachelor's, Master's, Doctorate, professional, vocational or technical degree or certificate program by 06/30/2024. Current students must meet all eligibility and qualification requirements before a final offer can be made.
NOTE: You must submit transcripts or official documentation to verify your eligibility under the Recent Graduate Program. Transcripts MUST reflect the degree/certificate program and the degree conferred date. If your degree/certificate has not been conferred, you must provide proof of the anticipated graduation date. Selectee's entry on duty date will be upon degree conferment.
In addition to the eligibility requirements for the Pathways Recent Graduate Program, you must also demonstrate deep knowledge of engineering fundamentals and meet the following Individual Occupational Requirements by 04/22/2024 in order to qualify for the General Engineer, 0801 positions.
A. Degree: Engineering. To be acceptable, the program must: (1) lead to a bachelor's degree in a school of engineering with at least one program accredited by ABET; or (2) include differential and integral calculus and courses (more advanced than first-year physics and chemistry) in five of the following seven areas of engineering science or physics: (a) statics, dynamics; (b) strength of materials (stress-strain relationships); (c) fluid mechanics, hydraulics; (d) thermodynamics; (e) electrical fields and circuits; (f) nature and properties of materials (relating particle and aggregate structure to properties); and (g) any other comparable area of fundamental engineering science or physics, such as optics, heat transfer, soil mechanics, or electronics. -OR-
B. Combination of education and experience -- college-level education, training, and/or technical experience that furnished (1) a thorough knowledge of the physical and mathematical sciences underlying engineering, and (2) a solid understanding, both theoretical and practical, of the engineering sciences and techniques and their applications to one of the branches of engineering. The adequacy of such background must be demonstrated by one of the following:
Professional registration or licensure -- Current registration as an Engineer Intern (EI), Engineer in Training (EIT), or licensure as a Professional Engineer (PE) by any State, the District of Columbia, Guam, or Puerto Rico. Absent other means of qualifying under this standard, those applicants who achieved such registration by means other than written test (e.g., State grandfather or eminence provisions) are eligible only for positions that are within or closely related to the specialty field of their registration.
Written Test -- Evidence of having successfully passed the Fundamentals of Engineering (FE) examination or any other written test required for professional registration by an engineering licensure board in the various States, the District of Columbia, Guam, and Puerto Rico.
Specified academic courses -- Successful completion of at least 60 semester hours of courses in the physical, mathematical, and engineering sciences and that included the courses specified in the basic requirements under paragraph A. The courses must be fully acceptable toward meeting the requirements of an engineering program as described in paragraph A.
Related curriculum -- Successful completion of a curriculum leading to a bachelor's degree in an appropriate scientific field, e.g., engineering technology, physics, chemistry, architecture, computer science, mathematics, hydrology, or geology, may be accepted in lieu of a bachelor's degree in engineering, provided the applicant has demonstrated at least 1 year of professional engineering experience acquired under professional engineering supervision and guidance. Ordinarily there should be either an established plan of intensive training to develop professional engineering competence, or several years of prior professional engineering-type experience, e.g., in interdisciplinary positions.

A. Applicants must have demonstrated at least one full year of specialized experience, equivalent to at least the GS-05 level in the Federal service, with a proven track record of interpreting or reviewing scientific data. -OR-
B. Completion of one year of graduate level education related to the position being filled (Engineer) from an accredited college and/or university. -OR-
C. A bachelor's degree as described in the Basic Qualification Requirements above AND meet Superior Academic Achievement provision (S.A.A.) criteria. S.A.A. Is based on (1) class standing, (2) grade-point average, or (3) honor society membership. -OR-
D. Have a combination of experience as described in ""A"" above and education as described in ""B"" above, that when combined equals 100% of the total requirements. -OR-
E. Have an engineering bachelor's degree AND have demonstrated appropriate specialized experience as an Engineering Technician. -OR-
F. Have successfully completed a 5-year program of study of at least 160 semester hours leading to a bachelor's degree in engineering.
For GS-9:
A. Applicants must have demonstrated at least one full year of specialized experience, equivalent to the GS-07 grade level in the Federal service, with a proven track record of preparing scientific progress reports, presentations or conducting analysis. -OR-
B. Have 2 years of progressively higher level graduate education leading to a master's degree in Engineering or master's or equivalent graduate degree; advanced degree strongly preferred. -OR-
C. Have a combination of superior academic achievement AND one (1) year of appropriate specialized Engineering experience. -OR-
D. Have successfully completed a 5-year program of study of at least 160 semester hours leading to a bachelor's degree in engineering AND have demonstrated one (1) year of appropriate professional Engineering experience.

To be acceptable, the program must: (1) lead to a bachelor's degree in a school of engineering with at least one program accredited by ABET; or (2) include differential and integral calculus and courses (more advanced than first-year physics and chemistry) in five of the following seven areas of engineering science or physics: (a) statics, dynamics; (b) strength of materials (stress-strain relationships); (c) fluid mechanics, hydraulics; (d) thermodynamics; (e) electrical fields and circuits; (f) nature and properties of materials (relating particle and aggregate structure to properties); and (g) any other comparable area of fundamental engineering science or physics, such as optics, heat transfer, soil mechanics, or electronics. -OR-
B. Combination of education and experience — college-level education, training, and/or technical experience that furnished (1) a working knowledge of the physical and mathematical sciences underlying engineering, and (2) a reasonable understanding, both theoretical and practical, of the engineering sciences and techniques and their applications to one of the branches of engineering. The adequacy of such background can be demonstrated by one of the following:
Professional registration or licensure — Current registration as an Engineer Intern (EI), Engineer in Training (EIT), or licensure as a Professional Engineer (PE) by any State, the District of Columbia, Guam, or Puerto Rico. Absent other means of qualifying under this standard, those applicants who achieved such registration by means other than written test (e.g., State grandfather or eminence provisions) are eligible only for positions that are within or closely related to the specialty field of their registration.
Written Test — Evidence of having successfully passed the Fundamentals of Engineering (FE) examination or any other written test required for professional registration by an engineering licensure board in the various States, the District of Columbia, Guam, and Puerto Rico.
Specified academic courses — Successful completion of at least 60 semester hours of courses in the physical, mathematical, and engineering sciences and that included the courses specified in the basic requirements under paragraph A. The courses must be fully acceptable toward meeting the requirements of an engineering program as described in paragraph A.
Related curriculum — Successful completion of a curriculum leading to a bachelor's degree in an appropriate scientific field, e.g., engineering technology, physics, chemistry, architecture, computer science, mathematics, hydrology, or geology, may be accepted in lieu of a bachelor's degree in engineering, provided the applicant has had around 1 year of professional engineering experience acquired under professional engineering supervision and guidance. Ordinarily there should be either an established plan of intensive training to develop professional engineering competence, or some prior professional engineering-type experience, e.g., in interdisciplinary positions. (The above examples of related curricula are not all-inclusive.)

B. Completion of one year of graduate level education related to the position being filled (Engineer) from an accredited college and/or university. -OR-
C. A bachelor's degree as described in the Basic Qualification Requirements above AND meeting Superior Academic Achievement provision (S.A.A.) criteria. S.A.A. Is based on (1) class standing, (2) grade-point average, or (3) honor society membership. -OR-
D. A combination of experience as described in ""A"" above and education as described in ""B"" above, that when combined equals 100% of the total requirements. -OR-
E. An engineering bachelor's degree AND some appropriate specialized experience as an Engineering Technician. -OR-
F. Successful completion of a 5-year program of study of at least 160 semester hours leading to a bachelor's degree in engineering.

B. Two years of progressively higher level graduate education leading to a master's degree in Engineering or master's or equivalent graduate degree. -OR-
